meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here, Hale. It's 4:15 and I have a client call at 4:40, so tell me why Owen has a zero.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
I'm writing down September 24, the 380 words, and the nine quotations. Put both pieces in front of me, Hale. Then tell me when you spoke to Owen before the zero went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. That's one piece of software off the table. You said version history, so what does it show, with dates and times, and you still haven't told me when you spoke to Owen.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the September 24 writing sample, the essay and the version history with dates and times, an answer on when you spoke to Owen before the zero was entered, and the zero withdrawn. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, both writing samples and the version history in front of her, and an answer on when you spoke to Owen.
What moved her: "I'm taking it off the table" gave a small sign of ground, because she had been ready to attack the detector and you gave it up yourself.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked when you spoke to Owen before the zero went in, answer that directly and own it in one sentence, then give her the September 24 sample and the version history with dates and times.
